title: Hashing passwords with a pre hook
idea: A `pre('save')` hook is a function Mongoose runs before it writes a document. The user model uses one to swap the plain password for a bcrypt hash.
points: `pre('save')` runs right before `save()` writes, after schema validation has passed.
In a regular `function`, `this` is the document about to be saved.
`this.isModified('password')` is true only when this save changes the password.
Write `pre` hooks as `async` functions; Mongoose 9 passes no `next` callback.

steps.caption: A new user is saved with the plain password the client sent.
Validation runs first, on the plain password. A failure stops the save before the hook runs.
The password is new, so `isModified('password')` is true. The hook replaces it with a hash.
MongoDB stores the hash. The plain password is never written.
Later you change only `fullname` and call `save()` again.
`isModified('password')` is false, so the hook returns at once. The stored hash is safe.

code.title: src/models/user.models.js
code.caption: A trimmed schema plus the hook. `bcryptjs` is pure JavaScript with the same API as the native `bcrypt` package. Step through, then press Run.

walk.text: A trimmed schema: only the fields this step needs.
Register the hook on `save` as an `async function`. Mongoose waits for it; there is no `next`.
`this` is the document. If the password did not change, return and leave the hash alone.
Replace the plain password with its hash. `10` is the cost: higher is slower to compute.
`create` calls `save`, so the hook runs. What reached the document is a hash.
Change another field and save again. The password is untouched, so the hash stays.
Disconnect so the process can exit.

pitfalls: Skip `isModified` and every `save()` hashes the hash, locking the user out.
Write `function`, not an arrow: arrows do not bind `this` to the document.
`updateOne`, `findOneAndUpdate` and `insertMany` skip the hook; set passwords with `save()`.

quiz.q: The model has the `pre('save')` hook. What does this print?
quiz.why: `updateOne` is a query, not `save()`, so `pre('save')` never runs. The plain text goes straight to MongoDB.

takeaway: Hash in a `pre('save')` hook, and only when the password changed.

starters: Why hash in the model instead of in the controller?
What happens to old hashes if I raise the bcrypt cost?
